# Shared fixtures of wall contract v1

CONTRACT.md (repo root) is the canon. These files are shared by the package
(`@submitator/badges`) and the server (submitator-backend, which vendors them
into `test/fixtures/badge_wall_v1/`). Every id and URL here is synthetic.

## vector.json

The RFC 8032 TEST 1 key (`test-rfc8032-1`), one signed payload with its
envelope, and the RFC 8032 TEST 1 empty-message signature. Both suites verify
it. Never edit it by hand: regenerate it together with the backend copy.

## walls/*.json

```
{ "name": string, "now": ISO 8601 UTC, "project": uuid, "payload": string,
  "expect": { "ok": boolean, "reason"?: string, "ids": (string | null)[], "skipped": number } }
```

- `payload` is the exact payload text (what the signature would cover).
- `now` is the clock to check expiry against.
- `expect.ids` are the ids of the badges the package keeps, in order. `null`
  stands for a kept badge whose malformed `id` was dropped.
- `expect.skipped` counts the badges the package leaves out.
- `expect.reason` (only when `ok` is false) is the package's wall-level reason:
  `payload` (not JSON, or not exactly the five keys with the right types),
  `version`, `project`, `timestamps` (malformed, impossible, or `issuedAt`
  not before `expiresAt`), `lifetime` (over 8 days), `expired`, `limits`
  (over 200 badges).
- `hand-*.json` are hand-written by the package: `node scripts/write-fixtures.mjs`
  builds them from `scripts/fixture-cases.mjs`, and a unit test checks that
  they match. `hand-skips.json` holds one bad badge per badge-level rule; the
  name of each says which rule it breaks.
- Walls generated by the server's tree builder (`bin/rails badge_wall:contract_fixtures`)
  sit next to them, with a `SOURCE` file naming the backend commit.

Package details the server can rely on:

- Root nodes are depth 1; a tree may be 16 levels deep.
- The node limit counts text nodes and elements alike.
- Lengths count characters (code points), not UTF-16 units or bytes.
- Spaces around a style value are dropped, not refused.

## envelopes/*.json

```
{ "name": string, "project": uuid, "now": ISO 8601 UTC,
  "publicKeys": { keyId: publicKey }, "body": string,
  "expect": { "ok": boolean, "reason"?: "envelope" | "too_large" | "key" | "signature" | "crypto" } }
```

`body` is the exact response body. They come from `scripts/write-fixtures.mjs`
too, signed with the test key.
